name: hra-atlas-browser
title: HRA Computational Model Atlas — organ selector + model-count gradient + subregion placement
question:
Can we present the full HRA-3D model-coverage picture as an interactive
atlas — pick any of the 50 GLB-backed HRA organs, see it colored by how many
mechanistic models are associated with it, browse straight to those
BioModels — AND go one level deeper, placing models at the specific organ
SUBREGIONS (anatomical structures) their cell types / FTUs resolve to,
rather than distributing every model uniformly across the whole organ?

study_card.goal: Build the atlas manifest from the BioModels->HRA map DB (the biomodel-hra-map study's reusable JSON) and, driving UP from each model's cell types + FTUs, place models at the specific organ subregions they belong to — falling back to the whole organ where no subregion resolves — then render it as a self-contained three.js organ browser where modeled subregions are colored and hoverable individually.
study_card.mechanism: ComputationalModelAtlas -> atlas_pack.build_and_write_atlas: organ->models from model_hra_map.json (organ Uberon -> [ids]), with organs grouped by the HRA anatomical-systems partonomy (12 systems) rather than a hand-curated map; atlas_subregions.place_models resolves subregions two ways — (1) ANATOMY: a Uberon the model itself carries (its FTU, ontology, or now gene-derived ASCT+B Uberons) that maps to a specific GLB mesh in the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk (datasets/hra_asctb_crosswalk.csv), placed under whichever organ's GLB contains that mesh; (2) cell-type ENRICHMENT: a model's cell type places it at an anatomical structure only where it is over-represented (>1.25x) vs the organ average in HRApop's per-AS cell populations (hra_pop.load_hrapop_as). Meshes are filtered to the organ by crosswalk organ_glb, and whole-organ-equivalent 'subregions' (label == organ) are skipped. build_atlas_manifest attaches per-organ `subregions` (node_names + Uberon + model list); the three.js viewer colors modeled subregions on a warm ramp over the organ's viridis base, with per-structure hover + click-to-list, and loads ALL same-sex GLBs per organ (bilateral L/R robustness so organs like kidney show both sides), plus a female/male switch and per-organ explode.
study_card.expected_result: All 50 organs selectable, grouped by the HRA anatomical-systems partonomy (12 systems); 19 modeled organs colored by count (blood 52 brightest); 9 organs additionally resolve 52 subregions — e.g. pancreas -> head of pancreas (16), intestine -> colon segments (caecum/transverse/ascending/descending/sigmoid colon, rectum, ~10 each), heart -> chambers (right ventricle 6, atria 5, interventricular septum 5) + great arteries, blood -> arterial tree, lung -> segmental bronchus (8), brain -> hippocampal formation (4) + olfactory bulb, kidney -> outer cortex (5), lymph node -> lymphatic vessels + medulla + follicle, trachea -> carina + cartilage — with the rest of every organ (and all other modeled organs, e.g. liver) falling back to the whole-organ color.
study_card.main_expert_question: Given HRApop's coarse anatomical-structure granularity and that most FTUs (islet, glomerulus, lobule) still have no 3D-crosswalk mesh, is anatomy-annotation (now including gene-derived ASCT+B Uberons) + enrichment-gated within-organ placement the right honest default (specific subregions; whole-organ fallback), or should we trade specificity for coverage (lower enrichment / cross-organ cell-type placement) to light up more structures?

biological_summary:
Mechanistic models cluster on a handful of organs (blood, pancreas, liver,
brain, intestine, heart) and leave most of the body's 3D anatomy unmodeled;
and within a modeled organ, most models describe organ-wide biochemistry, not
a specific sub-structure. This Atlas Browser makes both legible. It is now
generated from the (re-enriched) BioModels->HRA map DB (the biomodel-hra-map
study's reusable JSON) rather than the older name/annotation catalogs, giving
256 distinct models across 19 organs, and grouped by the HRA anatomical-systems
partonomy (12 systems: Cardiovascular, Digestive, Respiratory, Excretory,
Nervous, Lymphoid, Hematopoietic, Integumental, Reproductive, Entire Sense
Organ, Anatomical Structure, Other) rather than the old hand-curated 10-system
map. On top of the organ-level count gradient, it places models at specific
anatomical structures wherever the data supports it, two ways: (1) anatomy the
model itself carries — an FTU, ontology, or (newly) gene-derived ASCT+B Uberon
that maps to a specific GLB mesh in the ASCT+B crosswalk; (2) a cell type
placed at an anatomical structure only where HRApop measures it enriched above
the organ average. The big jump comes from the DB enrichment: the ASCT+B
gene->Uberon lever gave many models specific anatomical-structure Uberons that
resolve to GLB meshes, so the anatomy path went 8 -> 58 models. That resolves
64 models onto 52 subregions in 9 organs (58 via anatomy, 6 via cell type; 219
total placements) — e.g. pancreas head of pancreas (16), intestine colon
segments (caecum, transverse/ascending/descending/sigmoid colon, rectum, ~10
each), heart chambers (right ventricle 6, atria 5, interventricular septum 5)
+ great arteries, blood arterial tree (renal/mesenteric/splenic/hepatic
arteries), lung segmental bronchus (8), brain hippocampal formation (4) +
olfactory bulb, kidney outer cortex (5, cell-type enriched), lymph node
efferent/afferent lymphatic vessels + medulla + follicle, trachea carina +
cartilage — colored on a warm ramp so a modeled structure pops out of its
organ. Everything else falls back to the whole organ, which is still the
honest majority: HRApop's anatomical structures are coarse (gross regions, not
FTUs), and the curated FTUs themselves (islet, glomerulus, lobule, alveolus)
still have no 3D-crosswalk mesh — so liver, though heavily modeled, stays
whole-organ. The machinery is general: as the DB enrichment, HRApop coverage,
the 3D crosswalk, or per-model annotation improve, more subregions light up
automatically.
readouts: atlas manifest: n_organs (50), n_systems (12, HRA anatomical-systems partonomy), n_modeled (19), n_models_distinct (256), n_models_total (417), max_models (52), n_subregions (52), n_organs_with_subregions (9)
placement stats: n_subregion_models (64), n_anatomy_models (58), n_cell_type_models (6), n_placements_total (219)
per-organ n_models + BioModels list; per-organ `subregions` (node_names, Uberon, per-structure model list with placement `via`: anatomy | cell_type)

report.title: HRA Computational Model Atlas — 19/50 organs modeled, 64 models resolved to 52 organ subregions
report.objective:
Present HRA-3D model coverage as an interactive organ browser, and place
models at specific organ subregions (driven by their anatomy annotations +
cell types) where the data resolves them, falling back to the whole organ.
report.conclusion:
The atlas manifest covers all 50 GLB-backed HRA organs, grouped by the HRA
anatomical-systems partonomy (12 systems); 19 carry >=1 model (blood 52,
pancreas 51, liver 48, lung 43, thymus 43, spleen 34, brain 28, intestine
28, placenta 26, heart 15, spinal cord 9, trachea 8, main bronchus 7,
adipose 6, kidney 5, skin 5, ovary 4, lymph node 3, urinary bladder 2),
now sourced from the re-enriched BioModels->HRA map DB (256 distinct
models; thymus, placenta, spinal cord, trachea, and main bronchus are newly
modeled via the gene-derived anatomy). Subregion placement resolves 64
models onto 52 anatomical structures in 9 organs (58 via anatomy, 6 via cell
type; 219 total placements): pancreas -> head of pancreas (16), intestine ->
colon segments (caecum, transverse/ascending/descending/sigmoid colon,
rectum, ~10 each), heart -> chambers (right ventricle 6, atria 5,
interventricular septum 5) + great arteries, blood -> arterial tree
(renal/mesenteric/splenic/hepatic arteries), lung -> segmental bronchus (8),
brain -> hippocampal formation (4) + olfactory bulb, kidney -> outer cortex
of kidney (5, cell-type-enriched), lymph node -> efferent/afferent lymphatic
vessels + medulla + follicle, trachea -> carina + cartilage. Each modeled
subregion is colored on a warm ramp over the organ's viridis base and lists
its own models on hover/click; the viewer has bilateral L/R robustness, a
female/male switch, and per-organ explode. All other models — including
every model in the heavily modeled liver — fall back to the whole organ,
still the honest majority given the data.
report.caveat:
Subregion resolution jumped (64 models, 9 organs, up from 14/4) once the DB
enrichment (ASCT+B gene->Uberon) gave models specific anatomical-structure
Uberons that resolve to GLB meshes — but it is still bounded by the data,
not the method: HRApop's anatomical structures are coarse gross regions (so
a cell type rarely enriches in exactly one, hence only 6 cell-type
placements), and the curated FTUs themselves (pancreatic islet, glomerulus,
liver lobule, lung alveolus) still have NO 3D mesh in the ASCT+B crosswalk
to color, so heavily modeled liver stays whole-organ (pancreas now places at
the head-of-pancreas gross region, not its islet FTU). Placement is
enrichment-gated and, by default, within the model's tagged organ(s):
cross-organ cell-type placement is available but off, because the
mostly-generic cell types models carry (from the MeSH crosswalk) would
otherwise smear many models onto whichever organ has the most anatomical
structures.

findings.statement:
The atlas manifest enumerates all 50 GLB-backed HRA organs, grouped by
the HRA anatomical-systems partonomy (12 systems), and colors the 19
modeled ones by model count (blood 52 max, 256 distinct models), now
generated from the re-enriched BioModels->HRA map DB rather than the
older name/annotation catalogs — a whole-atlas overview of where
mechanistic modeling exists, each organ linking to its BioModels.

evidence.summary: 50 organs in 12 HRA anatomical systems, 19 modeled (256 distinct / 417 total), max_models=52 (blood); 31 organs greyed. Source: model_hra_map.json organ->models. Newly modeled via gene-derived anatomy: thymus (43), placenta (26), spinal cord (9), trachea (8), main bronchus (7).

findings.statement:
Driving placement up from the models' own anatomy annotations (now
including gene-derived ASCT+B Uberons) + cell types resolves 64 models
onto 52 organ subregions in 9 organs — pancreas head of pancreas (16),
intestine colon segments (~10 each), heart chambers + great arteries,
blood arterial tree, lung segmental bronchus (8), brain hippocampal
formation (4) + olfactory bulb, kidney outer cortex (5, cell-type
enriched), lymph node lymphatic vessels + medulla + follicle, trachea
carina + cartilage — replacing uniform within-organ distribution with
per-anatomical-structure coloring where the data supports it, and falling
back to the whole organ elsewhere.

evidence.summary: place_models: n_subregion_models=64 (n_anatomy_models=58, n_cell_type_models=6), 52 subregions in 9 organs, 219 total placements. The DB enrichment (ASCT+B gene->Uberon) drove the anatomy path 8 -> 58: gene-derived anatomical-structure Uberons resolve to crosswalk GLB meshes (pancreas head of pancreas, colon segments, heart chambers, lung segmental bronchus, brain hippocampal formation). Cell-type path (6, unchanged): kidney models' cell types enrich in the outer cortex (E>1.25 vs organ average).

limitations: The CELL-TYPE placement path is still bounded by HRApop's coarse anatomical-structure granularity (gross regions, not FTUs) — most cell types are spread evenly across an organ's structures and enrich in none, so only 6 models place via cell-type enrichment; the 58-model jump came from the gene-derived ASCT+B anatomy path, not from cell types.

The curated FTUs themselves (pancreatic islet UBERON:0000006, glomerulus, liver lobule, lung alveolus) still have NO mesh in the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk, so FTU-direct placement fires only for FTUs that do (lymph node follicle); pancreas now places at the gene-derived head-of-pancreas gross region rather than its islet FTU, and heavily modeled liver still stays whole-organ.

Cross-organ cell-type placement is off by default: the mostly-generic cell types models carry (from the MeSH crosswalk) are not specific enough to place a model into an organ it isn't tagged to without smearing many models onto the most-subdivided organs (colon, lung).

resolved_uncertainties: The Atlas Browser can be generated directly from the reusable BioModels->HRA map DB (biomodel-hra-map), grouped by the HRA anatomical-systems partonomy (12 systems), and can place models at specific organ subregions driven by their anatomy (including gene-derived ASCT+B Uberons) / cell types, not just at whole organs — realizing the fp-as-level-coverage follow-up.

The DB enrichment (ASCT+B gene->Uberon) drove the anatomy placement path 8 -> 58 models, so where the data supports it (pancreas head of pancreas, colon segments, heart chambers, lung segmental bronchus, kidney cortex, lymph-node vessels/follicle, brain hippocampal formation, trachea carina) per-anatomical-structure coloring replaces uniform within-organ distribution; where it does not (e.g. liver), whole-organ fallback is the honest and correct behavior.
remaining_uncertainties: Would an FTU->AS mesh crosswalk covering islet/glomerulus/lobule (or a finer HRApop-derived per-AS index) resolve the heavily modeled liver into subregions at its functional units, rather than the gross gene-derived regions the models place at now?
Can a stricter, cell-type-specificity-aware cross-organ gate light up multi-organ placement for genuinely cell-type-defined models without the generic-cell-type smear?

followup_study_proposals.title: An FTU -> 3D-mesh crosswalk so islet/glomerulus/lobule models place at their FTU
followup_study_proposals.motivation: The strongest subregion signal (a model's FTU) can't be shown for pancreas/liver/kidney-nephron because those FTUs have no ASCT+B-3D mesh — an FTU->representative-mesh mapping would place the largest modeled organs' models at their functional units.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Build/curate an FTU-Uberon -> GLB-node crosswalk (e.g. islet -> a pancreas-body region, glomerulus -> renal cortex), and place FTU models onto those meshes; measure the subregion coverage gain.

followup_study_proposals.title: Cell-type-specificity-gated cross-organ placement
followup_study_proposals.motivation: A model defined by a specific cell type legitimately maps to several organs; the current generic-cell-type signal smears, so cross-organ is off. A specificity score (how few organs a cell type occurs in) could re-enable it safely.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Weight each cell type by its cross-organ specificity in HRApop, and admit cross-organ placement only for models whose cell types are specific; compare against the within-organ-only default.
